# MachineChecked

> MachineChecked shows a mathematical paper beside its Lean 4 formalisation and says, claim by claim, what Lean establishes: which statements are linked to Lean declarations, whether Lean proves them (or the proof is incomplete, uses further axioms, or the declaration is missing), and which links still need a mathematician's review. It checks the Lean mechanically; it does not check that a Lean statement says what the paper says.

machinechecked.org hosts the reader and indexes published audits. An audit records what its author linked, checked and reviewed, under their name; the site does not endorse it.

## Use the tool

- [Getting started](https://github.com/cgarryZA/MachineChecked/blob/main/docs/GETTING_STARTED.md): run `machinechecked view` in a built Lean project with its paper (LaTeX, PDF, an arXiv URL, a leanblueprint or a formalization.yaml)
- [With a coding agent](https://github.com/cgarryZA/MachineChecked/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md): `machinechecked check --json` and the Agent Skill
- [Agent Skill](https://github.com/cgarryZA/MachineChecked/blob/main/skills/machinechecked/SKILL.md): what the statuses mean and what never to claim from them
- [Reviewing](https://github.com/cgarryZA/MachineChecked/blob/main/docs/REVIEWING.md): recording whether a Lean statement matches the paper
- [Evidence policy](https://github.com/cgarryZA/MachineChecked/blob/main/docs/EVIDENCE_POLICY.md): what each check does and does not establish

## Try it

- [Demo](https://machinechecked.org/demo/): a synthetic paper with a printed claim refuted in Lean and a corrected one proved
- [Source](https://github.com/cgarryZA/MachineChecked): Apache-2.0
